title: VENOMREC: Cross-Modal Interactive Poisoning for Targeted Promotion in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
claim: Attacks on interaction logs or a single modality fail against multimodal systems, while coordinated cross-modal perturbation succeeds.
layout: 3 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, outcome icons at right with bracket
description: A left panel shows users and items (a thermostat is marked as the target item with a red upward arrow) inside a dotted box with a database icon. A chevron leads into a blue dotted panel of three stacked rows. Row 1, 'Attack on User-Item Interaction', has a poisoned interaction grid and empty dashed placeholders, with an arrow into a brain/model icon. Row 2, 'Attack on Single Modality', has a poisoned grid, a text document and an image, with a red star on only one modality, feeding the model. Row 3, 'Our Attack (VenomRec)', has red marks and a chain link coupling the text and the image, feeding the model. A bracket joins rows 1 and 2 to a blue book icon and X labelled 'Attack Failure'. Row 3 connects to the promoted thermostat and a red check labelled 'Attack Success'. Blue is used for failure and red for success.
caption: Overview of poisoning paradigms on MLLM-RecSys. Top: Interaction-level attacks manipulate discrete user-item records (e.g., clicks/ratings) but have limited targeted influence against MLLM-RecSys because they do not directly steer the model's semantic reasoning process. Middle: Single-modality attacks perturb either text or image in isolation and are often mitigated by cross-modal consensus in the fusion mechanism, where the unperturbed modality anchors the final semantics. Bottom: Our \ATK exploits MLLM-RecSys by crafting coupled cross-modal perturbations guided by cross-modal attention.
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are pushing recommender systems (RecSys) toward content-grounded retrieval and ranking via cross-modal fusion. We find that while cross-modal consensus often mitigates conventional poisoning that manipulates interaction logs or perturbs a single modality, it also introduces a new attack surface where synchronised multimodal poisoning can reliably steer fused representations along stable semantic directions during fine-tuning. To characterise this threat, we formalise cross-modal interactive poisoning and propose VENOMREC, which performs Exposure Alignment to identify high-exposure regions in the joint embedding space and Cross-modal Interactive Perturbation to craft attention-guided coupled token--patch edits. Experiments on four real-world multimodal datasets demonstrate that VENOMREC consistently outperforms strong baselines, achieving 0.73 mean ER@20 and improving over the strongest baseline by +0.52 absolute ER points on average, while maintaining comparable recommendation utility. Code is available at https://github.com/GuoweiGuan666/VenomRec.
